case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

fault.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 154 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was redeployed at 17:10:29Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider is evidently still signing with the previous secret, so since about 17:10:45 the receiver rejects incoming webhooks as bad_signature and does not acknowledge them. Rejected webhooks never reach Kafka, so the ledger and confirmer never see those events. The provider keeps resending, and the bad_signature rate climbs from about 3.8/s to 22/s, a retry storm on top of new traffic. The count of unacknowledged webhooks therefore grows, and the money check cannot settle to its cutoff. That is the BooksBehindProvider alert. The queued rate fell from about 3.4/s toward 0 at the same moment and has no points after 17:11:00. Open points: I did not confirm which secret version the provider uses, and the rejections are not logged at WARN or ERROR (c3 was empty), so I cannot cite a log line. The timing and the bad_signature label make the cause very likely.

evidence.shows: All containers are running and healthy. Only webhook-receiver was recreated later than the rest, at 17:10:29Z, so the outage is not a crash.
webhook-receiver was deployed at 17:10:29Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, the only recent change. Every other service is unchanged since 17:09:03Z.

The bad_signature series starts at 17:10:45, right after the deploy, and climbs to 22/s. The queued series drops from 3.4/s and has no points after 17:11:00. Webhooks are being rejected for their signature instead of being put on Kafka.
No ERROR or WARN logs from webhook-receiver, so the rejections are not surfaced in logs. This is a logging gap, not evidence against the hypothesis.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its settings before the 17:10:29Z deploy, the previous WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION that matches the provider's signing key. The provider resends unacknowledged webhooks, so the backlog should then be accepted, queued and booked without a manual replay. Afterwards, run money_check to confirm the books settle. Coordinate any secret rotation so the receiver accepts both the old and new versions during the cutover. Also log signature rejections at WARN.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only webhook-receiver is recreated, so webhook intake pauses for a few seconds. The provider retries until acknowledged, so no events should be lost. After the restart, the resent backlog arrives as a burst, which raises Kafka traffic and consumer lag for a short time. The ledger consumer is idempotent and the confirmer works by our id, so duplicate deliveries should be harmless. If v2 was meant to block a compromised old secret, rolling back accepts that secret again.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Do this only once the provider is confirmed to sign with v2, or with the receiver accepting both versions.
